transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to call this meeting to order. As we all know, we're converting an unused office into a food pantry for our students and their households, and we're scheduled to open next month. Before we finalize the operating plan, I want to make sure we go through our standard implementation huddle and review the health and family-access details carefully. I've reviewed the draft plan, and I'd like to start by discussing the food storage and safety procedures, then move on to pickup logistics and language access. Does anyone have initial thoughts or concerns they'd like to raise?

transcript.text: I actually reviewed the county health guidance for the pantry this week, and there are some important requirements we need to add to the draft plan. The guidance specifies that refrigerated food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or colder, and the temperature needs to be logged every 2 hours while the pantry is open — not just a weekly check. It also requires that sealed packages display allergen labels. I have the printed guidance in my health-office binder and haven't yet incorporated it into the draft plan.
